case_name: Manohar Lal Alias Mannu and Another v State (Nct) of Delhi
petitioner: Manohar Lal Alias Mannu and Another
respondent:
State (Nct) of Delhi
Supreme Court of India

17 December 1999
Appeal (Cr.)  630-631 of 1999
The Judgment was delivered by : Hon'ble Justice K. T. Thomas
1. The carnage fuelled by the assassination of Indira Gandhi scored a heavy toll on the Sikh Community in Delhi and this case relates to a macabre which took place during then. Four sons of harbai were roasted to death in front of her eyes on 2.11.1984 at Trilokpuri in Delhi. The present appellants Jaggu and Mannu were tried before a Sessions Court for offences u/ss. 302 and 396 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code. The trial court convicted them of those offences and sentenced them to death on the first count and to life imprisonment on the next. A Division Bench of the High Court of Delhi confirmed the conviction and sentence. The appellants filed this criminal appeal by special leave,
2. PW-1. Harbai was the wife of Hooda Singh. They were living in an apartment situated at Trilokpuri. They
facts: The carnage fuelled by the assassination of Indira Gandhi scored a heavy toll on the Sikh Community in Delhi and this case relates to a macabre which took place during then.
Four sons of harbai were roasted to death in front of her eyes on 2.11.1984 at Trilokpuri in Delhi.
The present appellants Jaggu and Mannu were tried before a Sessions Court for offences u/ss. 302 and 396 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
Following the assassination of Indira Gandhi riots took place in different parts of Delhi and its impact reached Trilokpuri on 1-11-1984.
The mob caused nothing short of havoc.
issues: Whether the appellants were involved in the killing of the sons of PW-1
What was the appropriate sentence for the offence
petitioner_arguments: The endeavour was to show that PW-1 had gone to the extent of saying that the marauders killed even Shantibai, her daughter-in-law (wife of Darshan Singh) by burning her.
It might be that she had unwittingly formed such a wrong impression earlier at the first instance or that she herself is innocent of that part of the affidavit
respondent_arguments: The Division Bench of the High Court scrutinised the evidence afresh and concurred with the trial court regarding reliability of their testimony.
The law and order machinery had completely broken down.
court_reasoning: As seen above, during the early days of November, 1984, the Delhi witnessed worst of the carnage, following the assassination of Mrs. Indira Gandhi, preceded by large scale riots which had broken out then resulting into the killings of innocent persons irrespective of their age, middle aged or teenager of a particular community.
The situation Created by the anti-communal forces cannot be viewed lightly and needs to be dealt with sternly.
holding: Hence we are not persuaded to interfere with the finding that the appellants have committed the acts alleged against them.

Regarding the sentence, both sides addressed detailed arguments. The normal sentence for murder is life imprisonment and death penalty is now reserved to be given in 'rarest of the rare cases' in which the other sentence is unquestionably foreclosed vide Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, [1980] 2 SCC 684 1980 Indlaw SC 586.
The sentence for the offence u/s. 302 read with S. 149 of IPC is altered to imprisonment for life.
